blindSummary: No region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division - the research dossier lists it among the units with no sub-national signal, so the national evidence applies: the parliamentary women and family committee approved bills banning trans people from public restrooms in early 2025 (floor vote pending), and a national university's LGBTI rights observatory recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023, more than half of the homicide victims trans women (30 of 54). The absence of local findings reflects the country's lack of hate-crime statistics rather than any positive local difference.
blindSourceSummaries: A national newspaper (20 Feb 2025): the parliamentary women and family committee unanimously approved two sponsors' bills banning trans people from public restrooms, with exceptions for custody, medical need, and accompanying children under 12 or elderly/disabled persons, plus a ban on ambiguous bathroom signage; a floor vote is pending. Recounts a July 2023 complaint over 'feminine/masculine identity' bathroom labels at the country's main international airport and an LGBTI activist's objection that the measures weaponise stigma against trans people.

A university human-rights bulletin (15 April 2025): legal analysis of parliament's proposed prohibition of trans people from public restrooms, based on two 2023 bills fused at the women and family committee; contextualises it alongside the 2 April 2025 plenary approval (exempted from a second vote) of a law tightening rules on children's sexual education, framing the package as legalised discrimination against trans access to public space.

An LGBTIQ+ news agency (22 July 2024): a national university's LGBTI rights observatory annual report recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023 - more than half the homicide victims were trans women (30 of 54), with 19 killings in 2023 (12 trans women); documents torture-level violence, and a February 2023 case in which a criminal gang extorted sex workers (through forced 'protection' payments) in the capital's centre before murdering a 31-year-old sex worker in a district on the capital's outskirts. The country has no hate-crime law, so regional comparisons cannot come from official statistics.
